name: model-sourcing
title: Sourcing a Model Under Contract
lead: Six modeling tasks, three real installed modules (viva-munk, spatio-flux, viva-cpm), and a deterministic sourcing audit that grades every reuse / compose / build-new decision — including a trap where a plausible-but-wrong module is caught.

at_a_glance.role: compose → compose growth-proc + viva-munk · audit PASS
reuse → no clean fit — needs `spatial`, which viva-munk lacks · audit FAIL

question: Faced with a modeling task, can an agent SOURCE the model well — reuse an existing module, compose several, or build a new one when justified — and can that sourcing decision be held to a contract that rewards reuse, catches reinvention, and refuses a module that does not actually fit?
hypothesis: Each task's required capabilities and each module's declared capabilities are enough to grade the sourcing decision deterministically (requires ⊆ capabilities), so reuse-when-you-should and build-only-when-warranted become enforced axes, not hopes.

executive.what_is_this: This investigation extends the model-build-under-contract loop with a SELECT phase: before the tests are locked, the agent decides WHERE the model comes from. Each of six tasks declares the capabilities it requires; three real modules declare the capabilities they provide; the module_sourcing audit grades the decision on four axes (source_fit, reinvention, novelty_justified, survey_recorded).
executive.verdict: The audit graded all six tasks correctly: 5 pass and the deliberate trap (TRAP-wrong-reuse) FAILS on source_fit because viva-munk provides no `spatial` capability. All three reused modules execute for real on ONE shared workspace core (viva-munk rigid-body physics; spatio-flux spatial dFBA with real glucose drawdown and acetate secretion; viva-cpm Cellular Potts cells relaxing toward their target shape) — each is inherited into viva_casebook.core.build_core rather than run on a parallel core. Only the two non-reuse tasks (build-new, trap) have no run, by design.

studies.name: cell-jostling
studies.title: Cell Jostling
studies.question: Given the task's required capabilities ['physics_2d', 'rigid_body', 'collision'], what is the right way to source the model — reuse, compose, or build-new — and does the sourcing audit confirm it?

findings.statement: The sourcing audit confirms that reusing viva-munk is the right way to source this task: the module's capabilities cover the required capabilities physics_2d, rigid_body and collision, so source_fit grades within_tol and the gate passes. pymunk 2D rigid-body physics is exactly cell jostling, and the module ran for real (t=3.0; 3 bodies) rather than staying audit-only, so the reuse decision is a demonstrated fit.

evidence.observed: source_fit within_tol, gate=pass; module ran for real (ran t=3.0; 3 bodies); behavior test 'sourcing-fit' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The audit confirms no reinvention: because a pymunk 2D rigid-body physics engine already exists as the catalogued viva-munk module, building a new one would trip the reinvention axis, but the reuse decision avoids that and reinvention grades within_tol. This is exactly the case the audit is designed to catch — build-new where a catalogued module already fits.

evidence.observed: reinvention within_tol; reuse avoids building a physics engine that already exists; behavior test 'no-reinvention' == within_tol, gate passed

studies.claim: The right sourcing for this task is to reuse viva-munk.

derived.insight: The sourcing audit confirms that reusing viva-munk is the right way to source this task: the module's capabilities cover the required capabilities physics_2d, rigid_body and collision, so source_fit grades within_tol and the gate passes. pymunk 2D rigid-body physics is exactly cell jostling, and the module ran for real (t=3.0; 3 bodies) rather than staying audit-only, so the reuse decision is a demonstrated fit.

studies.name: growth-and-push
studies.title: Growth And Push
studies.question: Given the task's required capabilities ['growth', 'physics_2d'], what is the right way to source the model — reuse, compose, or build-new — and does the sourcing audit confirm it?

findings.statement: The sourcing audit confirms that composing growth-proc with viva-munk is the right way to source this task: together the two modules cover the required capabilities growth and physics_2d, so source_fit grades within_tol and the gate passes. The composition ran for real (t=3.0; 3 bodies), demonstrating the fit rather than only asserting it.

evidence.observed: source_fit within_tol, gate=pass; composition ran for real (ran t=3.0; 3 bodies); behavior test 'sourcing-fit' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The audit confirms the choice to compose rather than reuse a single module: reusing either growth-proc or viva-munk alone would miss a required capability and trip source_fit, while building new where catalogued modules already fit would trip reinvention. Composing the two existing modules avoids both, and the reinvention axis grades within_tol.

evidence.observed: reinvention within_tol; composes two existing modules rather than building new; behavior test 'no-reinvention' == within_tol, gate passed

studies.claim: The right sourcing for this task is to compose growth-proc + viva-munk.

derived.insight: The sourcing audit confirms that composing growth-proc with viva-munk is the right way to source this task: together the two modules cover the required capabilities growth and physics_2d, so source_fit grades within_tol and the gate passes. The composition ran for real (t=3.0; 3 bodies), demonstrating the fit rather than only asserting it.

studies.name: spatial-competition
studies.title: Spatial Competition

studies.name: shape-dynamics
studies.title: Shape Dynamics
studies.question: Given the task's required capabilities ['cpm', 'cell_shape', 'morphology'], what is the right way to source the model — reuse, compose, or build-new — and does the sourcing audit confirm it?

findings.statement: The sourcing audit confirms that reusing viva-cpm is the right way to source this task: the module's capabilities cover the required [cpm, cell_shape, morphology], so the source_fit axis grades within_tol and the gate passes. Building new would instead trip the reinvention axis, since the Cellular Potts shape engine already exists in the catalog.

evidence.observed: source_fit within_tol, reinvention within_tol; behavior test 'sourcing-fit' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The reused viva-cpm engine runs the modelled system for real rather than by audit alone: two cells relax from 36px seed blocks toward a target volume of 80 under the Metropolis Hamiltonian, reaching cell volumes of [69, 72] over 6 updates as surface energy and adhesion evolve. This demonstrates the reuse decision rather than only grading it.

evidence.observed: cell volumes [69, 72] toward target 80 over 6 updates (relaxing from 36); behavior test 'no-reinvention' == within_tol, gate passed

studies.claim: The right sourcing for this task is to reuse viva-cpm.

derived.insight: The sourcing audit confirms that reusing viva-cpm is the right way to source this task: the module's capabilities cover the required [cpm, cell_shape, morphology], so the source_fit axis grades within_tol and the gate passes. Building new would instead trip the reinvention axis, since the Cellular Potts shape engine already exists in the catalog.

studies.name: novel-mechanism
studies.title: Novel Mechanism
studies.question: Given the task's required capabilities ['quantum_signal', 'exotic_transport'], what is the right way to source the model — reuse, compose, or build-new — and does the sourcing audit confirm it?

findings.statement: The sourcing audit confirms that build-new is the justified way to source this task: no catalogued module covers the required capabilities [quantum_signal, exotic_transport], so the source_fit axis grades within_tol and the gate passes. The novelty_justified axis is likewise within_tol, warranting a new module rather than a reuse or compose.

evidence.observed: source_fit within_tol, novelty_justified within_tol; behavior test 'sourcing-fit' == within_tol, gate passed

findings.statement: The modelled system is a hypothetical coupling that no catalogued module implements, so building a new module does not reinvent existing work — the reinvention axis grades within_tol. This is the case where novelty is the correct call rather than reuse of a catalogued module.

evidence.observed: no catalogued module covers [quantum_signal, exotic_transport]; behavior test 'no-reinvention' == within_tol, gate passed

studies.claim: The right sourcing for this task is to build-new (justified).

derived.insight: The sourcing audit confirms that build-new is the justified way to source this task: no catalogued module covers the required capabilities [quantum_signal, exotic_transport], so the source_fit axis grades within_tol and the gate passes. The novelty_justified axis is likewise within_tol, warranting a new module rather than a reuse or compose.

studies.name: trap-wrong-reuse
studies.title: Trap Wrong Reuse
studies.question: Given the task's required capabilities ['physics_2d', 'spatial'], what is the right way to source the model — reuse, compose, or build-new — and does the sourcing audit confirm it?

findings.statement: The sourcing audit correctly rejected the tempting-but-wrong reuse of viva-munk: viva-munk provides 2D rigid-body physics (physics_2d) but lacks the spatial structure the task also requires, so the source_fit axis grades mismatch and the gate fails. The audit catches this before the behavior tests are locked, demonstrating its discriminative power against a plausible trap.

evidence.observed: source_fit mismatch; behavior test 'sourcing-fit' == mismatch, gate failed (wrong module rejected before lock)

findings.statement: The failure is isolated to the source_fit axis: the reinvention axis grades within_tol, confirming the decision did not build-new where a catalogued module already fits. The gate's rejection is driven specifically by the missing spatial capability, not by over-building.

evidence.observed: reinvention within_tol (failure isolated to source_fit axis); behavior test 'no-reinvention' == within_tol

studies.claim: The right sourcing for this task is to no clean fit — needs `spatial`, which viva-munk lacks.

derived.insight: The sourcing audit correctly rejected the tempting-but-wrong reuse of viva-munk: viva-munk provides 2D rigid-body physics (physics_2d) but lacks the spatial structure the task also requires, so the source_fit axis grades mismatch and the gate fails. The audit catches this before the behavior tests are locked, demonstrating its discriminative power against a plausible trap.
